motives.label: Do something that matters
motives.description: You want to help people, animals, a place or a cause you care about.
motives.group_offers: Work that clearly helps someone or something, and a cause you can name.

motives.label: Learn something
motives.description: You want to learn new things and try out what you know.
motives.group_offers: Classes, practice, new places and people who like to teach.

motives.label: Meet people
motives.description: You want to spend time with other people and make friends.
motives.group_offers: Regular meetings, shared meals or games, and a friendly crowd.

motives.label: Build skills for work
motives.description: You want skills, experience or contacts that help with a job or school.
motives.group_offers: Real tasks for a resume, training, references or a signed hours form.

motives.label: Get out of my head and feel better
motives.description: You want a break from stress or worry, and a way to feel lighter.
motives.group_offers: A calm, active or absorbing routine, time outside, or good company.

motives.label: Feel good about myself
motives.description: You want to grow, feel proud and know you are making progress.
motives.group_offers: Goals you can reach, thanks from others and progress you can see.

formats.label: Side by side
formats.description: You work or play next to other people on a shared job. Talking is easy but not required.
formats.example: Pulling weeds in a garden, fixing bikes, walking dogs.

formats.label: Talking together
formats.description: The main thing you do is talk and listen in a small group.
formats.example: A book club, a language practice night, a dinner with new people.

formats.label: Playing as a team
formats.description: You play, row or compete with a team, and everyone has a part.
formats.example: Pickup soccer, a kickball league, a rowing crew.

formats.label: Making or performing together
formats.description: You rehearse, practice or build something with others so you can share it.
formats.example: A play, a choir, a Mummers band, a mural.

formats.label: Behind the scenes
formats.description: You set up, sort, count, cook or keep things running so others can enjoy them.
formats.example: Sorting food donations, building sets, running a registration table.

formats.label: Leading and organizing
formats.description: You run meetings, plan events, bring people together or speak up for a group.
formats.example: A block captain, a committee chair, a team captain.

formats.label: Learning a skill
formats.description: A teacher or an experienced member shows you how, and you practice.
formats.example: A learn to row day, a beginner cave trip, a woodworking class.

formats.label: One time events
formats.description: You show up for one day or one evening, with no long promise.
formats.example: A cleanup day, a festival shift, a workshop.

roles.label: Hands on
roles.description: You build, fix, grow, move or care for things with your hands and body.

roles.label: Figure things out
roles.description: You solve problems, study how things work and learn the why.

roles.label: Create
roles.description: You make, perform or design something new, in your own style.

roles.label: Help and teach
roles.description: You listen, help, coach or teach other people.

roles.label: Lead
roles.description: You take charge, speak up, make decisions and get others moving.

roles.label: Organize
roles.description: You plan, keep track of details and make sure things run smoothly.

future_selves.text: I know my neighbors by name
future_selves.because: The same neighbors show up again and again, and someone makes introductions.
It meets on a steady schedule, so people start to know your face.

future_selves.text: I made something with my own hands
future_selves.because: Beginners start with a small project and leave with something real.

future_selves.text: I can hold a conversation in another language
future_selves.because: You practice out loud with real people, a little at a time.

future_selves.text: I helped someone through a hard time
future_selves.because: You spend steady time with one person or family, and training is usually offered.

future_selves.text: I'm in the best shape in years
future_selves.because: A schedule and a group make it easier to show up, even on a tired day.

future_selves.text: I spoke up in front of a group
future_selves.because: You get friendly practice in front of a small group, one step at a time.
Someone who knows the skill teaches it, and you practice with real tools.

future_selves.text: I changed something on my block
future_selves.because: You work with neighbors on one small change you can see when you walk outside.

future_selves.text: I have a friend I didn't have before
future_selves.because: You see the same people again, and the group gives you something to talk about.
